current_hypothesis: A new route to an explicit smooth Hamiltonian is to approximate the explicit square-slot witness by a structured composition of exact kick and drift Hamiltonian segments, using source-indexed smooth Gaussian kicks and global smooth drifts instead of the repository's old global polynomial ansatz.
stop_reason: Attempt 006 ruled out the witness-guided smooth kick-drift factorization: the emitted Hamiltonian was smooth and fast, but its audited k=10 ratio was only about 6.60e-05, so separable kick-drift fitting does not capture the toric branch geometry.

last_summary.worked: Implemented src/witness_guided_kick_drift.py, a new witness-guided Hamiltonian generator based on exact alternating kick and drift segments with smooth time windows. The script emits a real smooth Hamiltonian.py and supports training against the explicit square-slot witness from attempt_003. The emitted Hamiltonian benchmarked at about 0.340 seconds for a batch of 5000 points, well within the runtime constraint for single calls. Saved the training smoke-fit summaries and the end-to-end audit under results/research_loop/.
last_summary.did_not_work: The family failed decisively as a packing mechanism. The better of the two discrete smoke fits, using a radius-only loss, only reached surrogate ratio 0.00034465526940376647. When converted into the emitted smooth Hamiltonian.py and audited with RK4, the ratio dropped further to 6.601766155665936e-05 at radius 19.72808660462524 for k=10. That audited ratio is only about 0.53% of the repository's original polynomial baseline from attempt_001 and about 0.0106% of the toric square witness ratio 0.625.
last_summary.next_step: Drop separable kick-drift witness fitting. The next family should encode the branch geometry explicitly, most likely through an origami/folding or multi-chart generating-function construction rather than another smooth boundary-fitting flow factorization.
